title: I built a trading system that writes down what it expects the market to do, then grades itself on it. Here's where it actually stands.
author: Simone_Crosta
selftext:
Almost everything in this space is unverifiable by design. You're shown a screenshot and asked to believe it. I wanted something I could check instead.

I started trading at 15 and lost money. No CS background. Two years of building later, this is where I am.

The system writes one thesis per market before anything happens: where price should react, direction, target, and what would prove it wrong. Four agents contribute to it. It's a falsifiable prediction, not a signal.

That thesis gets tracked until it's confirmed, invalidated, or expired, and every ending is logged with a reason.

The part I care most about: the AI proposes, deterministic code disposes. The model reads the market, but a fixed rulebook decides whether entry conditions were genuinely met, and plain arithmetic sets size and risk. The AI is never told if a position is open or how the last trade went   it can't revenge-trade because it has no idea there was anything to avenge.

Current status, honestly: demo, three pairs, a handful of trades. Statistically meaningless and I'm not going to pretend otherwise. Code frozen since 28 July, untouched until 11 August, then I read the results.

It doesn't scale out, doesn't trail stops, doesn't have a plan B. Deliberate, not hidden.

It has broken several times. Each time the logs told me when, why and at what price, that's the whole point of building it this way.

Next step is a prop firm challenge on audited data.

Nothing for sale, no course, no signal group. Just posting the process as it happens.
